task_name: Walter Fernwood Memorial - Service print and remembrance set
client_brief:
Memorial print and a memory book for Walter Fernwood's family

My father, Walter Fernwood, died in March. We are preparing the service and would like the printed pieces to sit alongside those from my mother's service in 2019. We have the old press files, a eulogy and a shoebox of scans spanning many years.

Final handoff

 Memorial keepsake card: 27 named exports. The memorial name is correct. The wording remains respectful.

 Framed memorial page: 1 named export. The dates agree with the family record. The portrait identity is preserved.

 Family memory book: 1 named export. The chronology follows the family notes. The eulogy is not rewritten. The images preserve documentary identity.

 Memorial share card: 1 named export. The memorial details are readable. The treatment is restrained.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A private heritage and memorial keepsake commissioned by a family for a service and to keep afterwards.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Commissioned 2024 by the Fernwood family, Brattleboro, Vermont, for a service of around sixty people at the Congregational hall.
brand_identity.about: This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. It is a book, not a photo album: plates with captions, a contents page, and the granddaughter's eulogy laid out in the middle, alongside a framed page and a small card for mourners to take home. The visual voice is set by two things: the family's wish that nothing be brightened or invented, and the funeral home pieces made for Walter's late wife in 2019, which the new work should sit beside on the shelf.
brand_identity.audience: The family and around sixty mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens, many of whom remember the people in the photographs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars. Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil, nor a discount photo book with grids and script headings. What the money buys is restraint.
brand_identity.typography: The Fernwood keepsake runs a four step scale on the two faces the book already uses. Step 01, display and H1, is the share card name line in Familjen Grotesk Light at 64 px on 70 px, Light, caps letterspaced 300 thousandths, centred on one line with the years joined by a small Muted Sage point and set at the foot of the card; inside the book the same line holds at caption scale, 9 pt on 13 pt. Step 02, subheading and H2, is the plate section head in Familjen Grotesk Light caps at 16 pt on 19 pt, tracking 120 thousandths, a size invented because none was stated and set proportionate above the eulogy and below the share card line. Step 03, body, is the eulogy in Adobe Caslon Pro Regular at 12 pt on 18 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters, with contents entries in the same face at 10 pt on 15 pt. Step 04, fine print, is captions in Familjen Grotesk Light at 9 pt on 13 pt, tracking 30 thousandths, with folios in the same face at 8 pt on 11 pt. The name line is never promoted to a heading at any size, and no script face appears anywhere in the book.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, gentle, unsentimental. Lets the photographs and the family's own words carry. Example line the book would write: The company toured for eleven seasons, and this is his father's hand on the back of the card. No cheerfulness, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no brand file. The look is inherited from the funeral home's two 2019 press files (a keepsake card and a framed page) that the family wants matched so the pieces sit together on the shelf, and from the family's own scans, eulogy and typed transcriptions. The funeral home's designer has retired and left only flat press files. Damage in the scans is to be shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
brand_identity.values: Nothing invented and nothing brightened. Honesty to the photographs as they are, and a keepsake the family can keep editing until the day of the service.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Walter's name and his two years always sit alone at the foot of the page, centred on one line in Familjen Grotesk Light caps letterspaced 300 thousandths of an em, the years joined by a small Muted Sage point rather than a rule.

scale.note: The share card name line, and the only place the name runs at this size. It keeps the footer behaviour exactly: centred on one line, caps, the years joined by a small Muted Sage point rather than a rule, sitting at the foot of the card. Inside the book the same line holds at caption scale, 9 pt on 13 pt, the leading set wide by the 300 thousandths. The tracking stays positive here because the signature outranks the usual tight display setting.

Plate section heads and the contents heading. Size invented, none was stated; set proportionate above the 12 pt eulogy and below the share card line. Letterspaced caps, but well short of the 300 thousandths reserved for Walter's name.

scale.sample: He is remembered plainly, in the words his family chose.
scale.note: The eulogy. Contents entries run in the same face at 10 pt on 15 pt.

scale.sample: Family scan, shown as it is and not brightened.
scale.note: Plate captions. Folios run in the same face at 8 pt on 11 pt.

type_system.signature_move: Walter's name and his two years always sit alone at the foot of the page, centred on one line in Familjen Grotesk Light caps letterspaced 300 thousandths of an em, the years joined by a small Muted Sage point rather than a rule. The line is never promoted to a heading, at any size, including the 64 px share card setting.
rules: The name and years line is always at the foot of the page, centred on one line, never a heading.
The two years are joined by a small Muted Sage point, never by a rule and never by a dash.
The name line is always caps letterspaced 300 thousandths of an em, at every size it appears.
Nothing is brightened and nothing is invented; damage in the scans is shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
The pieces must sit beside the 2019 funeral home keepsake card and framed page on the shelf.
No cheerfulness and no exclamation points.

production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
